text:
alex: Heads up — cluster-autoscaler kept flip-flopping yesterday between gpu-pool-west and burst-cpu-pool. A bunch of GPU jobs got restarted mid-run. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria: saw the alerts. pods bounce for ~2-3 min then reschedule. looks like scale-up completes then we immediately scale-down one of the new nodes. :confused: 

suresh: likely too-aggressive scale-down + expander choice. what flags are we running for CA currently?

alex: baseline flags from k8s/helm chart: --expander=most-pods --scale-down-unneeded-time=2m --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 --balance-similar-node-groups=true --max-empty-bulk-delete=3

dave: Oof. 2m is tiny for GPU workloads (container/cold-start + mounting volumes). Couple quick ideas:
- bump --scale-down-unneeded-time to 15m
- switch expander to --expander=least-waste (favours packing GPUs together)
- raise --max-empty-bulk-delete to 10 so CA can be more efficient when there really are empty nodes
- set --max-node-provision-time=10m (so scale-up latency isn't considered failed too early)

jen: also watch for PDBs and local-storage. If pods have PDBs CA won't evict them which can make it look like nodes are in-use inconsistently. do we have undocumented PDBs for training jobs?

maria: yes some training jobs have PDB=1. and many jobs mount local scratch via hostPath for performance. that makes scale-down more conservative.

suresh: couple more flags to consider: --skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true (leave as default) but if most jobs use hostPath we should annotate nodes we never want to delete: kubectl annotate node <n> cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true for debug.

dave: also check balance-similar-node-groups vs expander combo. with mixed spot/preemptible pools we were getting CA oscillation because it preferred cheapest nodes but then newer jobs required non-preemptible GPUs. If you can tag nodegroups with a priority label we can use node group sizes+descheduler policies to reduce churn.

suresh: sample CA invocation I'd try in canary (v=4 logs):
```
cluster-autoscaler --cloud-provider=aws \
  --expander=least-waste \
  --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m \
  --scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.4 \
  --max-empty-bulk-delete=10 \
  --max-node-provision-time=10m \
  --balance-similar-node-groups=true \
  --skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false \
  -v=4
```

alex: interesting — why set skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false? isn't that risky?

dave: default true avoids deleting nodes with system pods. setting false lets CA consider them if system pods are moveable (we run kube-system as DaemonSets that tolerate eviction). only do if you audited system pod eviction + node prep scripts.

jen: another thing: node drain timeouts and CSI attach/detach delays cause CA to overestimate node emptiness and then re-add. check kubelet and attach-detach-controller logs for slow detach of GPU-attached volumes. bumping --max-graceful-termination-sec might help.

maria: we also saw higher latency to attach ENIs in us-west-2 last week; that caused scale-up to be slow -> CA would retry different pool -> more churn. region infra noise + aggressive flags = bad combo.

suresh: action plan:
1) roll a canary CA with flags above in staging cluster for 24h
2) run synthetic GPU job churn (short training jobs) to exercise scale-down path
3) audit PDBs/local-storage and annotate the handful of nodes we want to protect
4) if still noisy, try switching expander back to most-pods but disable balance-similar-node-groups to see behaviour

alex: sounds good. I'll spin up the canary CA tomorrow morning and post logs. tagging @infra-bot to schedule canary deploy.

infra-bot: scheduled canary deploy for cluster-autoscaler at 2024-06-18T09:30Z (canary: ca-canary-2). Logs will stream to #eng-infra.

dave: when you post logs include the CA decision traces (v=5) and output of "kubectl get nodes -o wide" so we can correlate provisioning timestamps.

alex: will do. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
